messages:
diane.l: Hi team  I had a telemedicine consult with a EU provider last night (video call, doctor is based in Lisbon). They invoiced me 65 EUR and I paid with Amex. Clinic now says they need a 'policy endorsement code' or a pre-auth number to file directly with the insurer. They also want the provider's NIF/VAT and IBAN on the invoice. Can People Ops/Benefits generate a short proof of coverage or an authorization number I can give them? Also need to know what to upload for HSA and whether Amex receipts are acceptable. Thanks!

leo.benefits: Sorry you had to deal with that. Quick answers: we don't issue pre-auth numbers for telemedicine retroactively, but we can produce a proof-of-coverage/authorization letter that includes policy number, claims intake email/phone, and a brief statement authorizing the provider to contact the insurer. That often satisfies clinics who ask for a pre-auth. For HSA: an itemized invoice + proof of payment (Amex statement or receipt) is fine.

claims_bot: Auto-note: Submit international telemedicine/digital claims at https://benefits.redwood.com/claims -> "International reimbursement". Required: itemized invoice, proof of payment (card stmt screenshot accepted), date/time of consult, provider legal name, VAT/NIF if available, currency, and exchange rate record. Typical processing 2-6 weeks.

jon.claims: Concrete tip: ask the provider to email their invoice and bank details (IBAN/VAT) to claims@redwood.com and include your member ID in subject. If they email us we can attach the provider invoice directly to the claim and attempt direct billing. The phrase that helps is: "Patient authorizes provider to communicate with insurer and submit invoice for payment."

leo.benefits: Copy/paste letter I can send as a PDF (you can hand to provider):
```
Redwood Inference - Benefits Claims
Policy #: RW-PL-2039
Member: Diane L. (Member ID: 0043219)
Claims intake: claims@redwood.com
International claims phone: +1-800-555-0199 (multilingual support, limited hours)

To whom it may concern,

This letter confirms that the above-named individual is an active member of Redwood Inference's medical plan. The employer authorizes the provider to contact the insurer for verification of coverage and to submit invoices for direct billing where insurer policy allows. This letter is not a guarantee of payment.

Please email invoices and banking details to claims@redwood.com for processing.

Sincerely,
Redwood Benefits Team
```

marta.hr: If this consult was during company travel or client work, upload a calendar invite or travel proof when you submit and mark the claim "business travel" to request expedited review. Also DM me if you'd like People Ops to call the provider in Portuguese to confirm they emailed claims.

diane.l: Thanks everyone. One follow-up: provider asked if the insurer accepts electronic invoices (e-invoice). Some EU clinics will only accept official e-invoices. Do we accept PDFs sent by clinics?

jon.claims: Yes, PDF invoices are accepted. If they request an e-invoice number, ask them to include their internal invoice reference and send PDF copy — insurer accounting can reconcile with IBAN/VAT. If they insist on a special e-invoice format, ask them to email claims@redwood.com and we will coordinate.

leo.benefits: I will generate the PDF letter and DM it to you within the hour. Also add a short Portuguese line: "Por favor envie fatura e detalhes banc1rios para claims@redwood.com" so clinic sees the email.

diane.l: Appreciate it. Uploading Amex receipt + invoice to the portal now. Will DM if provider calls claims line. :pray:
